packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-11 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond the stated rules: I listed the packet directory to learn image filenames (packet.json not opened), and I made enlarged (2.5x), grayscale, auto-contrast copies of the tiles in my scratchpad and read them alongside the originals. No web, search, edition or catalogue was consulted.
- Note: several phrases on face 1 look like they may match familiar scriptural wording; I have NOT filled anything from memory. Where I recognised a phrase, I transcribed only the letters I can see and flagged uncertain letters.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two overviews: image-001 (face 1) and image-005 (face 2). One narrow vertical parchment strip, c. 2.5 cm wide by c. 13 cm tall against the ruler, held by glass weights. Tiles: 002/003/004 = face 1 top-to-bottom; 006/007/008 = face 2 top-to-bottom; consecutive tiles overlap by about 2-4 lines.
- Script: gothic textualis (formal book hand), dark brown/black ink, heavy abbreviation. Clearer than a cursive; letter forms mostly readable where ink survives.
- Face 1: about 34 lines. Lines are cut on the RIGHT (words run off the edge); the left edge appears to be at or near the left boundary of the text column (lines begin with whole words). At the top, separated from the main block by a blank line-space, are two lines beginning with a paragraph mark (image-002 ll.1-2), possibly the end of the preceding section or a heading-like citation line; I cannot tell which. In the lower part of image-004 (left edge) there are letter traces belonging to ANOTHER column to the left ("...sac", "...m", "ag..."), so the leaf was written in at least two columns and this strip includes the intercolumn.
- Face 2: lines are cut on the LEFT; the right ends of lines survive and are followed by blank margin, so this face shows the end of a column plus margin. A vertical fold/band on the left side of face 2 is whiter and its letters are crisper. Near the bottom right of face 2 (image-008 lower right) there is a small ruled frame/box in the margin containing a few letters ("h..vc"[?] over "ge"[?]), possibly a marginal note or a catchword-type entry; unread. Faint traces of further letters at the extreme right edge of face 2 may belong to an adjacent column.
- No rubrics or enlarged initials visible apart from the paragraph mark at image-002 l.1. One word in image-006/007 appears underlined ("m(e)i"?).
- Tentative interpretation (not observation): continuous Latin prose, apparently sermon-like or expository, quoting gospel-style phrases ("in euang(eli)o hodiern(o)") and a citation "Jere. xlvi". 

LIMITATIONS
- Right-hand loss on face 1 and left-hand loss on face 2 remove several letters to a word or more per line. Face 2 is badly faded/abraded in the middle and lower parts; my readings there are weak. Overlapping tile lines are flagged, not repeated as new text.
- Line numbers count from the top of each tile image.

SPANS SELECTED
1. Face 1, whole surviving column: image-002 ll.1-17, image-003 ll.3-16, image-004 ll.4-17.
2. Face 2, image-006 ll.1-13 and image-007/008 (weak).
Unread: most of the middle of face 2; the boxed marginal entry on face 2.
